objective: The selected next step of CRYSTAL-UP-20261108-001 (G1, question 9; backlog B4), started on 2026-11-08: a challenge of A12, that bond distance (the size of the least knot through two distinctions, minus one) is a law's own spacing. Alternatives: chain distance counted in knots (the fewest knots in a chain from one distinction to the other, each sharing a distinction with the next) and counted in distinctions (the fewest distinctions in such a chain's union). Discriminator: prove what each does on parity laws, whose knots are the circuits of size at least three of a binary matroid, then compute both beside bond distance on the laws measured since 2026-11-07 and on non-matroidal laws in hand. Frozen before anything runs: A12 is confirmed for a class of laws if on it every chain measure either collapses (no spacing at all) or equals bond distance up to an additive constant; it is overturned if some law has a chain measure that is a non-degenerate spacing and changes a dimension or a circle shape that bond distance reads.
status: Complete 2026-11-08: the first challenge of A12. On parity laws chains of knots add nothing to bond distance (counted in knots they collapse to one step, counted in distinctions they equal it; proved by matroid connectivity). Off parity laws the measures part exactly at gates, where one value of a shared distinction satisfies both knots (72 of 1,156 gluings of three-place knots; clause chains spanned exactly when they chain as implications); the NAND thread is a chain-distance line with no bond distance. By its frozen test A12 is overturned as a universal statement; it holds wherever knots compose, covering every law measured for space, and A38 replaces it. Next: Research directions, selected two bits per tile with products first (B8), awaiting a go-ahead.
stop_rule: Stop when A12 is confirmed for the matroidal laws and every non-matroidal law in hand is decided, or at the first law where a chain measure changes a dimension or a circle.
